title: fix(desktop): serialize and harden vault writes (audit LIB-B1/B8/B10, SHOT-B3)
body:
## What changed and why

Two concurrent writes to the same vault item could lose an update, reject each other with `ENOENT`, or leave a truncated sidecar, and a failed screenshot overwrite could destroy the original PNG. This closes audit findings **LIB-B1** (high), **LIB-B8**, **LIB-B10** and **SHOT-B3**, following plan `04-sidecar-write-serialization` (Batch 2, parent NIW2-382).

- **New `main/library/atomic-write.ts`**: a module-level per-key async mutex (`withLock`), unique temp names, and an fsync'd `atomicWriteFile`. The lock is module-scoped because `currentVault()` builds a fresh `LibraryVault` per IPC call, so a per-instance lock would not span callers.
- **`LibraryVault.writeMeta` and `ensureIdentity`** now take the lock keyed by the sidecar path and read-merge-write inside it. The per-instance `identityInFlight` guard is gone: the lock plus a re-read inside it covers LIB-B8. `remove()` takes the same lock so a racing `writeMeta` cannot recreate a sidecar just after it is deleted.
- **`writeImage`, `writeThumbnail`, `writeCursorTrack`, the tag registry and the video edit-session files** use `atomicWriteFile`. Screenshots use the `.part` suffix, which is not in `ALL_EXTS`, so a half-written shot stays invisible to `list()`.
- **`saveScreenshotToVault`**: when a *new* screenshot's sidecar write fails, the PNG is removed so the caller's retry cannot save it again under a second id and leave an orphan. An overwrite keeps its PNG.

## Deviations from the plan

- **Task 5 is in `main/screenshots/screenshot-save.ts`, not `screenshot-ipc.ts`.** The save sequence moved into `saveScreenshotToVault` after the plan was written. Because that function only needs `../library`, I tested it with a mocked vault instead of leaving it manual-only: `screenshot-save.test.ts` (fails without the fix, passes with it).
- **The 40-writer test asserts 40 distinct fields**, not just valid JSON, to match Review Focus 1 ("all 40 fields").
- **The "keeps the original" `writeImage` test fails differently than the plan predicted.** In a read-only directory the old `writeFile` does not truncate the PNG; it writes through the existing file's permissions and overwrites it. The test still separates the behaviours: old code resolves and overwrites, new code rejects and keeps the original.
- **The plan file and its `00-index.md` row are not deleted here.** Both exist only on `docs/code-audit-2026-10-15` (PR #301, still open), not on `main`. Whoever merges #301 second should drop the plan 04 file and its index row.

## How I verified it

Run from `apps/kaipu-record` unless noted.

- Race tests first, confirmed failing on the old code: `ENOENT` on `clip.json.tmp`, five different `assetId`s for one item, and a lost title.
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/library/library-vault.test.ts src/main/library/library-vault.hash-retry.test.ts`, run 3 times: 30/30 each time.
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/library src/main/recording`: 193 passed.
- `bun run check-types`: green.
- `CI=1 bun run verify` from the repo root: **two consecutive green runs** (260 files, 2251 tests in `kaipu-record`).
  - An earlier run had one failure, `capture-overlay.test.tsx` ("answers copy from the Copy button and from ⌘C…"), which timed out at 10 s while turbo ran 12 tasks in parallel. It passed 3 of 3 in isolation, this PR changes nothing under `src/renderer`, and it passed in both later full runs. It looks like a timing flake under load; I did not investigate it further.
- I ran `bun install --frozen-lockfile` first, because this worktree's `node_modules` was missing `better-auth` and type checking failed in `browser-sign-in.ts` (a file this PR does not touch).
- Not run: the Playwright desktop E2E suite (CI runs it), and the manual steps below.

## How to test it yourself

1. In the Library, open an item's tag field and paste `design, demo, ` (two tags at once). Open `<vault>/.kaipu/<id>.json`: it must be valid JSON containing both tags. (Plan 17 fixes the UI assigning only the last tag; this PR guarantees the file stays intact.)
2. Rename an item three times quickly. The title shown and the sidecar must agree, with no `*.tmp` or `*.part` left in `.kaipu/`.
3. Screenshot → edit → Save → Overwrite twice. `<vault>/<id>.png` must be the latest edit, with no `.part` files in the vault root.

Refs NIW2-390

Run: Gas City session ni-wisp-u1z8wr5, bead ka-9t3, Mac mini
